name: spoken-word-cleanup
title: Spoken-word clean-up
description: Version 2. The reference workflow (docs/spec/reference-workflows/audacity-spoken-word-cleanup.md), automated and adaptive: remove the DC offset, reduce noise using the quietest steady region as the profile, flatten every persistent tonal line until none stands out, bring the peak to -1 dBFS, and optionally compress. Every value is measured on the clip it is replayed on.

steps.title: Remove the DC offset
steps.rationale: Audacity step 3: remove the DC offset first, so every later measurement is centred.

steps.title: Reduce noise (profile from the quietest steady region)
steps.rationale: Audacity step 4: the quietest part of the clip, using the shortest sample that works, applied across the whole clip.

steps.title: Flatten the tonal lines
steps.rationale: Audacity steps 5-6: find every line running through the clip, including its speech pauses, and cut each until it matches the surrounding material; repeat until no peak stands out. A peak that is only there while someone talks is part of the voice and is left alone.

steps.title: Bring the peak to -1 dBFS
steps.rationale: Audacity steps 2-3: the +30 dB amplify and the normalise become one gain measured on the clip. It runs after the reductions, which move the peak by hundredths of a dB, so the -1 dBFS target is exact at the end and the final limiter has nothing to do. (In Audacity the level comes first so the waveform is visible; here the view zooms instead.)
